title: Following a lead's own stated prerequisite makes the lead unreachable
body:
An engine-internal string is shown to the player as guidance:

    "No authored choice is currently available in this journey state."

That is a sentence about the content graph, not about the world. It tells a player
nothing they can act on, and it names concepts ("authored", "journey state") that exist
nowhere in the game's own vocabulary.

Worse is when it appears. The charter-backlog event lead printed its own prerequisite:

    "Required first: talk to Rowan Quill."

I talked to Rowan Quill. In the very same response, that lead changed to the string
above. Following the game's explicit instruction is what made the lead unreachable.

Reproduced independently in two sessions by two players (a live-test QA lead, and a
reference-tier claude-opus-5 session). Both hit it on the Albany opening.

Two separable problems:
  1. The lead becomes unreachable after satisfying its own stated prerequisite — that is
     either a content-graph gap or a prerequisite that does not describe the real gate.
  2. Whatever the cause, an unreachable lead should say something a player can use, not
     surface the authoring layer's own vocabulary.

evidence.summary: Reproduced in two independent sessions; also surfaces an engine-internal string as player guidance.
